q: A memoryless system is y = x^2 (sample values). Feeding the single sample x = 28 + 200 gives output:

f: Step 1: summed input = 228. Step 2: y = (228)^2 = 51984. Check: separate outputs would sum to 40784, which differs, proving nonlinearity.

q: For x(t) = u(t) and h(t) = u(t) in a continuous-time LTI system, y(89) is: (spaced-repetition variant 16877)
h: The output is the ramp r(t) = t u(t).
f: Step 1: y(t) = integral from 0 to t of 1 dt = t for t at least 0. Step 2: y(89) = 89. Check: differentiating y returns u(t), the step response relationship h = ds/dt holds.

q: X(s) = 309 / (s (s + 86)). The final value x(infinity) is:
h: Final-value theorem: limit of s X(s) as s tends to 0.
f: Step 1: s X(s) = 309/(s + 86). Step 2: at s = 0 this is 309/86 = 3.593. Check: the remaining pole at -86 is in the left-half plane, so the theorem applies.

q: y[n] - 0.3774 y[n - 1] = x[n]. The pole of H(z) is at z =
h: Transform: Y(z) (1 - a z^-1) = X(z); the pole solves 1 - a z^-1 = 0.
f: Step 1: H(z) = 1 / (1 - 0.3774 z^-1). Step 2: denominator zero when z = 0.3774. Check: this matches the pair a^n u[n] with a = 0.3774.

q: A sawtooth-type Fourier series has harmonic coefficients b_k = 2A/(k pi). For A = 158 and k = 37, b_k is:
h: Substitute A and k into 2A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: b_k = 2 x 158 / (37 pi). Step 2: = 2.7185 (4 decimal places). Check: coefficients fall as 1/k, slower than a triangle wave (1/k^2) but faster than the constant spectrum of an impulse train.

q: A DFT uses N = 1024 samples taken at fs = 796672 Hz. The bin spacing is: (spaced-repetition variant 16877)

f: Step 1: ratio = 2.78. Step 2: 10 log10(2.78) = 4.44 dB. Check: ratio 0.5 gives about -3 dB and ratio 10 gives +10 dB; sign follows gain versus loss.

q: A 16-ary modulation runs at 784 baud. Its bit rate is:
h: Bit rate = baud x log2(L).
f: Step 1: bits per symbol = log2(16) = 4. Step 2: bit rate = 784 x 4 = 3136 bps. Check: denser constellations raise rate at fixed baud but need higher SNR for the same error rate.

q: For A = [[0, 1], [-608, -496]] (companion form), det(A) is:
h: det [[p, q],[r, s]] = p s - q r.
f: Step 1: det = (0)(-496) - (1)(-608). Step 2: = 608. Check: det(A) equals the product of eigenvalues, here the constant term of s^2 + 496 s + 608.

q: For x(t) = 105 cos(2 pi 110 t) (1 ohm reference), the average power P is:
h: P = A^2 / 2 for any sinusoid, independent of frequency.
f: Step 1: identify amplitude A = 105. Step 2: P = A^2/2 = 11025/2 = 5512.5. Check: average of cos^2 over a period is 1/2, and frequency 110 Hz does not change the average.

q: Evaluate the integral over all t of (t^2 + 369) delta(t - (-391)) dt:
h: Sifting: the impulse samples the bracket at t = t0.
f: Step 1: sifting property: integral of x(t) delta(t - t0) dt = x(t0). Step 2: x(-391) = -391^2 + 369 = 153250. Check: everything away from t = -391 is multiplied by zero.

q: The system y[n] = x[n] + x[n - 632] is classified as: (spaced-repetition variant 16878)
o: Memoryless and noncausal
With memory and noncausal
Memoryless and causal
With memory, causal, linear and time-invariant
h: It uses the present sample and a past sample only.
f: Step 1: x[n - 632] is a past sample, so the system has memory. Step 2: no future samples appear, so it is causal. Step 3: it is a fixed linear combination with constant coefficients, hence linear and time-invariant.

q: Convolving x[n] = {852, 636} with h[n] = {146, 434} (both starting at n = 0), the value y[1] is:
X(s) = 1 / ((s + 326)(s + 693)) with causal ROC. In x(t), the coefficient multiplying e^(-326 t) is:
h: Cover-up: set s = -a in 1/(s + b).
f: Step 1: partial fractions: A/(s+326) + B/(s+693) with A = 1/(693 - 326) = 0.0027. Step 2: x(t) = (0.0027 e^(-326 t) - 0.0027 e^(-693 t)) u(t). Check: x(0+) = 0, matching the initial-value behaviour of this strictly proper X(s).

q: x[n] = (0.9212)^n u[n]. The sample x[3] is:
h: Cube the base; u[3] = 1.
f: Step 1: x[3] = (0.9212)^3. Step 2: = 0.7817. Check: |a| = 0.9212 is below 1, so the ROC |z| above 0.9212 includes the unit circle: decaying and stable.

q: An odd square wave of amplitude 276 has sine harmonics (4A/(k pi)) sin(k w0 t) for odd k. The amplitude of the k = 21 harmonic is: (spaced-repetition variant 16878)

f: Step 1: amplitude = 4 x 276 / (21 pi). Step 2: = 16.734 (4 decimal places). Check: it falls as 1/k, so higher harmonics weaken - the origin of Gibbs ripple concentration near jumps.

q: A 1090 Hz tone is sampled at fs = 1126 Hz. It aliases to:
h: Fold: alias = |f - k fs| for the integer k giving a result in [0, fs/2].
f: Step 1: Nyquist needs fs at least 2180 Hz, so 1126 Hz undersamples. Step 2: alias = |1090 - 1 x 1126| = 36 Hz. Check: 36 lies in [0, 563], the representable baseband.

q: Bandwidth B = 772 kHz and SNR = 1 dB. The Shannon capacity is approximately (bps): (spaced-repetition variant 16878)
h: C = B log2(1 + SNR), with SNR converted from dB first.
f: Step 1: SNR linear = 10^(1/10) = 1.259. Step 2: C = 772000 x log2(1 + 1.259) which is about 907591 bps. Check: Shannon is an upper bound; a practical rate must stay below it, then Nyquist sets the levels.

q: AM with modulating bandwidth BWm = 192.6 kHz has total transmission bandwidth: (spaced-repetition variant 16878)
h: AM keeps both sidebands: BWt = 2 x BWm.
f: Step 1: sidebands sit at fc +/- up to 192.6 kHz. Step 2: BWt = 2 x 192.6 = 385.2 kHz. Check: SSB would need only 192.6 kHz, at the cost of sharper filtering.

f: Step 1: lambda^2 + (11) lambda + (-1160) = (lambda - (29))(lambda - (-40)). Step 2: eigenvalues are 29 and -40. Check: sum of roots = -11, product = -1160, matching trace and determinant relations.

q: Total energy of x(t) = e^(-136 t) u(t) (1 ohm reference) is: (spaced-repetition variant 16879)

f: Step 1: 11 t - 4389 = 11 (t - 399). Step 2: compression by 11 with shift right by 399. Check: the common wrong answer is 4389, the unfactored constant.

q: The system y(t) = 59 x(t) + 663 is:

Time-varying but linear

Linear: it is a straight-line graph

f: Step 1: with x(t) = 0 the output is 663, not 0. Step 2: superposition fails, so the system is nonlinear (affine). Check: the term 59 x(t) alone would be linear; the offset 663 breaks it.

q: H(s) has denominator s^2 + (208) s + (10791), i.e. poles at s = -99 and s = -109. For the causal system: (spaced-repetition variant 16879)

f: Step 1: poles are -99 and -109. Step 2: both are negative, so the causal ROC (right of the rightmost pole) includes the jw axis: stable. Check: zeros do not decide stability.

f: Step 1: |pole| = 0.471 is below 1. Step 2: the causal ROC outside the pole therefore includes the unit circle: stable.
